source.title: The Future of Large Language Model Pre-training is Federated
source.authors: Lorenzo Sani; Alexandru Iacob; Ze-Yu Cao; Bill Marino; Yan Gao; Tomas Paulik; Wanru Zhao; William F. Shen; Preslav Aleksandrov; Xin-Chi Qiu; N. Lane

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates in-context learning scores for models of different sizes, bearing on downstream performance scaling (V6), but does not fit or test the pretraining-loss scaling laws themselves.
record.gate_note: The paper cites scaling laws and uses Hoffmann et al.'s token-to-parameter ratio to select training amounts, but those cited results and the chosen ratios are not tests of the laws. The rows below are the paper's own downstream benchmark scores by Photon model and task.
record.test_reason: The study is a federated-training systems paper. It uses Hoffmann et al.'s 20 tokens/parameter ratio only to plan training budgets (Table 1). Its own results compare federated with centralized training and report its own Photon models' benchmark scores. The in-context-learning tables (Tables 5–6) are a sanity check of three Photon models (1B, 3B, 7B). They do not fit a relationship, test predictability, or relate scores to pretraining loss. The models also differ in token budgets and training recipe, so model size is not isolated. No version of the claim is tested as stated.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly wrong. The authors say Photon's downstream performance scales as expected with model size and that the largest model wins 10 of 14 comparisons. Their own table captions say 6 of 7 and 5 of 6, which is 11 of 13. Their main conclusions concern federated pretraining: it matches or beats centralized perplexity, with the gap favoring federated at larger sizes. It is also robust to data heterogeneity and partial participation. They make no claim about scaling laws themselves.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies federated pretraining and downstream evaluation rather than fitting the original scaling-law methodology. It uses Hoffmann et al.'s token-to-parameter recommendation as a planning input.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream scores vary by benchmark; some are non-monotonic with model size.

fits_no_version.finding: Downstream ICL scores of three federated Photon models (1B, 3B, 7B) mostly rise with size: 11 of 13 tasks are best at 7B. BoolQ declines and StrategyQA is flat.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream benchmark scores of federated-pretrained LLMs rise with model size, as in centralized training (no fit; token budgets confounded).

record.problems: The downstream comparison includes only Photon-1B, Photon-3B, and Photon-7B; no uncertainty estimates are reported. Scores are non-monotonic on some benchmarks, and the paper's stated count of 10 out of 14 comparisons does not align with the 13 benchmark columns shown in Tables 5 and 6.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows were retained for pretraining cross-entropy/perplexity curves: those results compare federated and centralized training or optimizer choices, and do not test a power-law relationship or any other listed version.

untested.parts: No power-law fit of loss against parameters, tokens or compute.
The Chinchilla ratio is adopted, not tested.
Text-only federated pretraining; no power-law fit in another regime.
No fitted relation or predictability test. Only three model sizes with confounded token budgets; no scores related to loss.

record.verdict_notes: Federated systems paper; the scaling-law citations motivate the work and set token budgets (Table 1). The perplexity curves (Figs 3, 9) compare federated with centralized training per size, not loss against scale. The Table 6 header order in the extracted text is scrambled, so the per-column assignment of COPA, MMLU and StrategyQA values is uncertain. The record's T2/tests classification and its V6 labels are withdrawn.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit or test of held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute.
No small-run fit is used to predict larger-run loss.
The paper adopts a token-to-parameter ratio from Hoffmann et al.; it does not determine the loss-minimizing parameter/token allocation over compute budgets.
No controlled comparison of architecture shapes at fixed parameter count.
Experiments are text pretraining; no other modality or listed training regime is tested.
Tests in-context learning scores across model sizes, not predictions from a fitted relationship or downstream performance conditioned on pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal splits under alternative fitting choices.

relation.reason: The study uses the 20 tokens/parameter recommendation with vocabulary adjustments; its experiments evaluate federated training rather than test the stated scaling-law versions.

tranche.reason: Section 6.4 assumes Hoffmann et al.'s allocation rule to plan training. Tables 5–6 evaluate Photon utility across three sizes, without fitting or validating a downstream scaling prediction.

source_check.notes: Table 6 places COPA before MMLU; four sampled rows swap these columns. Section 7.9 reports 10 wins out of 14, whereas Tables 5–6 show 11 wins out of 13.
